title: Renewal Offer Issuance Standard for Lease Term Agreements
content:
Renewal offers are delivered only on a Lease Term Agreement that is current. This standard sets when revenue management delivers renewal offer lines on an expiring term, which lines are delivered, when none are delivered and how each line's offered rent is priced.

## 1. Delivery

1.1 **Current term only.** Renewal offers are delivered only on a term that is current; the term's status on its record decides this.

1.2 Offers are delivered the expiring program's offer lead time in calendar days before the term end date: one line for each term program in the expiring program's renewal offer options, each open for the program's offer validity days. A program whose offer lead time is 0 receives no offers.

1.3 No offer is delivered while a notice to vacate is on file, while the lease is in default or has an eviction filed, or, when the program requires renewal only with no past-due balance, while the lease has a past-due balance; such a term converts to month-to-month at its end unless the resident gives notice.

## 2. Pricing an offer line

2.1 *Retired clause.* The clause "the 12-month-equivalent renewal rent may exceed the in-place contracted rent by no more than the effective cap: the expiring program's renewal increase cap, less its loyalty reduction when the loyalty tenure is met, and never more than the statutory increase cap for the community's state where one exists" is **no longer in force**, together with the maximum renewal rents it defined (the in-place contracted rent raised by that cap, or by that cap less the loyalty reduction, rounded half up to the cent); it has been superseded by the current basis for the cap on renewal offer lines.

2.2 Each offer line's offered rent is the 12-month-equivalent rent adjusted by the offered program's rent adjustment (with its minimum monthly premium as a floor for a premium), rounded half up to the cent.

2.3 Revenue management may offer less than the cap; an offer above the cap is an offer posted in error and is corrected before acceptance.

## 3. Statutory increase caps by state

| Community state | Statutory increase cap |
|---|---|
| California | 8.8 percent (0.088) |
| Washington | 9.68 percent (0.0968) |
| Colorado, Texas, Georgia, Arizona | none |

## Delivery decisions — illustrations (hypothetical)

| Situation of an expiring term | Offers delivered |
|---|---|
| Current Standard Lease (10-12 Months) term, no notice on file, lease active, no past-due balance | Yes — one line per offered program, 90 days before the end date |
| Same term with a notice to vacate on file | No — the term converts to month-to-month at its end unless the resident gives notice |
| Same term while the lease has a past-due balance | No |
| Current Month-to-Month Agreement | No — its offer lead time is 0 |
| Term already superseded | No — the term is not current |

superseded_clauses: The 12-month-equivalent renewal rent may exceed the in-place contracted_rent by no more than the effective cap: the expiring program's renewal_increase_cap_pct, less loyalty_increase_cap_reduction_pct when the loyalty tenure is met, and never more than statutory_increase_cap_by_state for the community's state where one exists.
